text:
This looks like mid-2018. Fed funds at 1.91% matches May/June 2018 (the effective rate was 1.91% in May and June). Headline CPI at 2.8% YoY matches May 2018 (2.8%), and core CPI at 2.2% is consistent. Unemployment at 4.0% fits May 2018 (3.8%) less well, but April 2018 was 3.9%, so the 4.0% may reflect a data vintage or a different measure. The 10-year yield at 2.98% fits May 2018, and the 2-year at 2.66% also fits.

Equity returns show US large caps up 3.7% over the month, which fits May 2018 (S&P +2.4%) and June (+0.6%), though not perfectly. Gold fell 2.2% in the month, which fits May 2018 (-1.3%) roughly. The emerging-market 6m return of -10.7% is consistent with mid-2018. Of the two, May 2018 looks more likely given the 10-year yield, but the equity 1m return of +3.7% might instead point to a late-May snapshot.

The 3m change in the dollar is +7.83, which fits the April-May 2018 dollar rally. I will go with May 2018.
